gen-gf-gowun-dodum-fs-literata: Friendly and plain-spoken, Gowun Dodum draws its crossbars as heavy as its stems, with curve tips that stop short of touching. Literata follows in serif form, its strokes swelling and thinning like soft ink.
gen-gf-gruppo-fs-literata: Gruppo lets white space leak into its letters freely, giving headings a light, modern feel. And Literata, a classic serif, grounds them with thin lines that still carry real weight.
gen-gf-gudea-fs-literata: Literata brings sturdy thin strokes and slightly heavier thick ones, with curves that open wide. Literata sits under Gudea's monoline heading, where every stroke keeps one line from start to finish and the c tips stay apart.
gen-gf-gulzar-fs-bespoke-sans: Literary with a shimmer, Gulzar swells gently on its curves so the weight shifts subtly across each word. Bespoke Sans keeps its own lines low in contrast, and that quiet is the pair's sharpest quality.
gen-gf-gupter-fs-bespoke-sans: Editorial and a bit clipped, Gupter packs its stems close with medium stroke contrast. Bespoke Sans gives the text generous space where curves meet the stem, so if the heading feels tight, nudge the body size up for more breathing room.
gen-gf-hahmlet-fs-bespoke-sans: Hahmlet's wide-eyed lowercase e is its giveaway, and its diagonals look gently pressed thinner than the verticals. Bespoke Sans, a sans-serif, stays low in contrast beneath it.
gen-gf-hanken-grotesk-fs-literata: Approachable from the first line, Hanken Grotesk keeps a constant-width stroke with bowls open like a tipped ladle. Literata, a classic serif, then carries a longer read with sturdy thin strokes and restrained thick ones that never tire the eye.
gen-gf-harmattan-fs-literata: Wiry and tightly spaced, Harmattan draws every letter like pipe cleaner, with an open e showing a clear gap. Literata, a text serif, offsets it with a modest stem-to-hairline ratio, and that wire-versus-ink difference is the strongest thing here.
gen-gf-host-grotesk-fs-literata: Host Grotesk leaves a wide slot between the two ends of its c and keeps stroke contrast low. But Literata, a text serif, does the sustained work, with middle-of-the-road contrast and wide, unclosed curves.
gen-gf-hubballi-fs-literata: Hubballi has a ruler-and-compass feel, its ink strokes tapering out before they touch and its letters set close together. And Literata, a classic serif, adds the restrained thick-thin play of a worn wooden stamp.
